episodes.174746: Monsoonal flow led to several days of thunderstorms October 7 and 8. Riverside County saw the highest impacts, with several reports of small hail, funnel clouds and a landspout tornado.
episodes.174779: A Tropical Upper Tropospheric Trough combined with an approaching tropical wave. The wave enhanced the moisture content in the atmosphere, and with the instability aloft, conditions became favorable for showers and thunderstorms development across the area.
episodes.175014: A couple waterspouts formed in association with a lee island cumulus line extending west-southwest of the Lower Florida Keys.  Lower tropospheric ridging was becoming established across the eastern United States, resulting in the beginning of lower tropospheric east-northeast winds across the Florida Keys and an increase in lower tropospheric moisture.

events.narrative: Broadcast Media reported several tourists were swept away by a water surge in Charco La Soplaera in Penuelas. Emergency managers were able to rescue them.

An EF-0 landspout occurred from Menifee to Southern Canyon Lake along Highway 78. The landspout tracked across mostly open space before dissipating near I-15. Minor damage reported. Half inch hail was also reported.
Several reports of a funnel cloud near Romoland and Menifee between 3-4 pm.
Four downed trees in Menifee from thunderstorm wind gusts (measured at 40-46 mph). Two trees were dead.

events.county: Hawk Channel From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To The Reef
events.narrative: Two waterspouts were observed south southwest of Key West via the office rooftop cameras.  Both waterspouts had narrow condensation funnels extending one-third the way to the water surface.
